description: I am Amina Zafar- specialized in Environmental Sciences. I welcome you to join my team for Earth System Trend Detective Challenge. Lets do it together to learn, build and impact something amazing
summary: My project is an interactive open science observatory, focuses water-crop stress in Shakargarh, one of the most fertile land of Pakistan. Using 44 years of FLDAS (Famine Early Warning Systems Network Land Data Assimilation System) data for evapotranspiration and soil moisture measurements cross validated with 1-km MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) earth observation (NDVI) for 25 years, I developed this interactive observatory. There is autocorrelation-corrected Mann–Kendall significance tests (p < 0.05) employed.  Because of the past flood episodes and intensified monsoons, the land in Shakargarh, appears to be getting wetter on the average but the observatory reveals the progressive aridification in winters, and explains the real problem of SKG is too little water retention in winters. With the help of seasonal diagnostics and time series analysis, the project helps in informed decision making and sustainable water management for both farmers and govt.
details: Open Science web observatory provides an interactive dashboard to analyze the evapotranspiration and soil moisture variables separately as well as their relation, with interpretation of graphs and statistical analysis. This user friendly tool helps understanding the monsoon spell that excessively waters the land in summer, however, yet leaves too little soil moisture retention in winter. While the surface averages apparently shows no water stress in Shakargarh, but our seasonal analysis unveils progressive aridification. It helps farmers to make informed decisions, like they can protect their soil moisture through mulching or laser land leveling. To built the project, NASA's open data sources: Giovanni (FLDAS Model for ET& SM data) and NASA AppEEARS (MODIS Satellite Data for crop cover) were used, and statistical pipeline in Python was developed in Google colab before deploying streamlit app, backed by GitHub public repository. Then built a Streamlit app and GitHub repository. Instead of relying on rainfall, the lands soil moisture was connected with seasonal calendar across three agriculture belts in Shakargarh. Vedio made using Canva demonstrates the project and Presentation explains the graphical presentation and their significance.
